(a) "Community Health Outreach" shall mean the provision of basic health services, health education, and referral services at community level, including but not limited to immunization, antenatal care, family planning, and management of common childhood illnesses;

(b) "Community Health Workers" (CHWs) shall mean individuals trained and certified by the Kano State Primary Health Care Management Board to provide basic health services within their communities;

(c) "Local Government Areas" (LGAs) shall mean the administrative units within Kano State where outreach activities shall be conducted;

(d) "Target Communities" shall mean the specific communities listed in Annex A to this Agreement;

(e) "Program Period" shall mean the period of twelve (12) months commencing on 1st March 2018 and ending on 28th February 2019, unless extended or terminated in accordance with the provisions of this Agreement.

1.2 In the interpretation of this Agreement, words importing the singular shall include the plural and vice versa; words importing one gender shall include all genders; and headings are for convenience only and shall not affect the interpretation of this Agreement.

**ARTICLE 2: SCOPE OF WORK**

2.1 LLI shall plan, organize, and implement community health outreach activities in not less than twenty (20) Target Communities across five (5) LGAs, namely: Kano Municipal, Fagge, Dala, Tarauni, and Gwale.

2.2 The scope of work shall include:

(a) Mobilization of community members for health services utilization;

(b) Deployment of trained Community Health Workers and outreach teams;

(c) Provision of health education on maternal and child health, nutrition, hygiene, and disease prevention;

(d) Support for routine immunization activities in collaboration with the State Primary Health Care Management Board;

(e) Referral of complicated cases to designated primary health care facilities;

(f) Collection and reporting of routine health data as per Ministry-approved formats.

2.3 LLI shall conduct outreach sessions on a monthly basis in each Target Community, subject to security, climatic, and other operational considerations.

2.4 The Ministry shall provide technical oversight, facilitate access to health facilities, and ensure that LLI activities align with State health policies and guidelines.

**ARTICLE 3: BUDGET AND FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

3.1 The total budget for the implementation of this Agreement shall be Fifty Million Naira (₦50,000,000.00) only, as detailed in the Budget Plan attached as Annex B.

3.2 The budget shall be allocated as follows:

(a) Personnel costs (including CHW stipends and outreach team allowances): 40%;

(b) Operational costs (including logistics, transportation, and outreach materials): 35%;

(c) Health education materials and supplies: 15%;

(d) Monitoring and evaluation: 10%.

3.3 LLI shall submit a detailed budget breakdown to the Ministry for review and approval before the commencement of each quarter.

3.4 Any adjustment to the budget allocation shall be made by mutual written agreement of the Parties and recorded as an amendment to this Agreement.

3.5 The Ministry shall facilitate the timely disbursement of funds to LLI through the Kano State Ministry of Health budget line for NGOs and development partners, subject to the availability of funds and compliance with State financial regulations.

**ARTICLE 4: REPORTING OBLIGATIONS**

4.1 LLI shall submit to the Ministry:
(f) Ensure that all personnel engaged under this Agreement adhere to the Ministry's code of
conduct and professional standards.

2.2 LLI shall submit a quarterly work plan to the Ministry at least fourteen (14) days before
the commencement of each quarter, detailing the proposed outreach schedule, target communities,
and resource requirements.

2.3 LLI shall participate in monthly coordination meetings convened by the Ministry and shall
provide updates on progress, challenges, and emerging issues.

**3. ROLES AND RESPONSIBILITIES OF THE MINISTRY**

3.1 The Ministry shall provide overall technical oversight and strategic direction for the
community health outreach activities. In this capacity, the Ministry shall:

(a) Review and approve the quarterly work plans submitted by LLI, and provide feedback within
ten (10) working days of receipt;

(b) Facilitate access to public health facilities and communities, including the issuance of
necessary introductions or letters of authorization to local government authorities and
community leaders;

(c) Provide technical guidance and reference materials to ensure that health education content
is accurate, up-to-date, and consistent with State health policies;

(d) Coordinate with other government agencies and development partners to avoid duplication of
efforts and to maximize the impact of outreach activities;

(e) Participate in monitoring visits to outreach sites, as necessary, to assess the quality and
reach of activities.

Kano State Ministry of Health has_mou_reference MOU-KSMOH-2018-003. Record status: current.

3.2 The Ministry shall designate a focal person within the Department of Public Health who
shall serve as the primary point of contact for LLI for operational and technical matters.

3.3 The Ministry shall keep LLI informed of any changes to State health policies, guidelines,
or priorities that may affect the implementation of the activities under this Agreement.

**4. JOINT ACTIVITIES**

4.1 The Parties shall jointly undertake the following activities to enhance the effectiveness
and sustainability of the community health outreach program:

(a) **Joint Planning and Review Sessions:** The Parties shall hold quarterly review sessions to
assess progress against targets, review monitoring data, and identify areas for improvement;

(b) **Community Engagement Forums:** The Parties shall jointly organize community engagement
forums in Target Communities to raise awareness about the outreach program, solicit feedback
from community members, and foster local ownership;

(c) **Capacity Building:** The Ministry shall facilitate the participation of LLI personnel in
relevant training programs organized by the Ministry or its partners, including training on data
management, disease surveillance, and community mobilization;

(d) **Monitoring and Evaluation:** The Parties shall jointly develop and implement a monitoring
and evaluation framework, including agreed indicators, data collection tools, and reporting
templates. Joint monitoring visits to outreach sites shall be conducted at least once per
quarter;

(e) **Knowledge Sharing:** The Parties shall share relevant reports, publications, and lessons
learned from other programs to inform the implementation of this Agreement.

4.2 The Parties agree that all joint activities shall be documented, and minutes or summary
reports shall be prepared and shared with both Parties within fourteen (14) days of the
activity.
**ANNEX C: DISPUTE RESOLUTION, FORCE MAJEURE, AND GENERAL PROVISIONS**

**5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

5.1 The Parties shall use their best efforts to resolve amicably any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, through direct negotiation between the designated focal persons.

5.2 If the dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of the date either Party delivers written notice of the dispute to the other, the matter shall be referred to the respective Permanent Secretaries or their designees for a further period of thirty (30) days of facilitated discussion.

5.3 If the dispute remains unresolved after the period specified in Clause 5.2, either Party may refer the matter to mediation administered by the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, Nigeria, Kano Branch, in accordance with its Mediation Rules in effect at the time of the referral. The mediation shall be conducted in English and held in Kano, Kano State, unless the Parties agree otherwise.

5.4 Any dispute not settled by negotiation or mediation within ninety (90) days from the date of the initial written notice may be finally settled by arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Cap A18, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator appointed by mutual agreement of the Parties, or, failing such agreement within twenty-one (21) days, by the President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, Nigeria. The seat of arbitration shall be Kano, Kano State, and the language of the proceedings shall be English. The award of the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding on the Parties.

5.5 Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction in Kano State to protect its confidential information or intellectual property pending the resolution of any dispute under this Clause 5.

5.6 The obligation to pay any amount due and payable under this Agreement shall not be suspended or delayed by reason of any dispute, except as otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

**6. FORCE MAJEURE**

6.1 Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any failure or delay in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement, other than an obligation to pay money, if such failure or delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event.

6.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, a "Force Majeure Event" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party, including but not limited to: acts of God; flood, drought, earthquake, or other natural disaster; epidemic or pandemic; act of terrorism or civil unrest; war or threat of war; fire or explosion; strikes or industrial action; and any law, regulation, order, or directive of any governmental authority that materially affects the performance of this Agreement.

6.3 The affected Party shall, as soon as reasonably practicable but in no event later than seven (7) days after the commencement of the Force Majeure Event, notify the other Party in writing of the nature of the event, its expected duration, and the obligations affected.

6.4 The affected Party shall use all reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable. The Parties shall consult with each other to agree on reasonable alternative arrangements to minimize the impact of the Force Majeure Event on the implementation of the activities.

is accurate, up-to-date, and consistent with State health policies;

efforts and to maximize the impact of outreach activities;

reach of activities.

3.2 The Ministry shall designate a focal person within the Department of Public Health who

**4. JOINT ACTIVITIES**

4.1 The Parties shall jointly undertake the following activities to enhance the effectiveness
and sustainability of the community health outreach program:

(a) **Joint Planning and Review Sessions:** The Parties shall hold quarterly review sessions to
assess progress against targets, review monitoring data, and identify areas for improvement;

(b) **Community Engagement Forums:** The Parties shall jointly organize community engagement
forums in Target Communities to raise awareness about the outreach program, solicit feedback
from community members, and foster local ownership;

(c) **Capacity Building:** The Ministry shall facilitate the participation of LLI personnel in
relevant training programs organized by the Ministry or its partners, including training on data
management, disease surveillance, and community mobilization;

(d) **Monitoring and Evaluation:** The Parties shall jointly develop and implement a monitoring
and evaluation framework, including agreed indicators, data collection tools, and reporting
templates. Joint monitoring visits to outreach sites shall be conducted at least once per
quarter;

(e) **Knowledge Sharing:** The Parties shall share relevant reports, publications, and lessons
learned from other programs to inform the implementation of this Agreement.

4.2 The Parties agree that all joint activities shall be documented, and minutes or summary
reports shall be prepared and shared with both Parties within fourteen (14) days of the
activity.

**5. DISPUTE RESOLUTION**

5.1 The Parties shall use their best efforts to resolve amicably any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or invalidity thereof, through direct negotiation between the designated focal persons.

5.2 If the dispute is not resolved within thirty (30) days of the date either Party delivers written notice of the dispute to the other, the matter shall be referred to the respective Permanent Secretaries or their designees for a further period of thirty (30) days of facilitated discussion.

5.3 If the dispute remains unresolved after the period specified in Clause 5.2, either Party may refer the matter to mediation administered by the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, Nigeria, Kano Branch, in accordance with its Mediation Rules in effect at the time of the referral. The mediation shall be conducted in English and held in Kano, Kano State, unless the Parties agree otherwise.

5.4 Any dispute not settled by negotiation or mediation within ninety (90) days from the date of the initial written notice may be finally settled by arbitration in accordance with the Arbitration and Conciliation Act, Cap A18, Laws of the Federation of Nigeria, 2004. The arbitral tribunal shall consist of one (1) arbitrator appointed by mutual agreement of the Parties, or, failing such agreement within twenty-one (21) days, by the President of the Chartered Institute of Arbitrators, Nigeria. The seat of arbitration shall be Kano, Kano State, and the language of the proceedings shall be English. The award of the arbitral tribunal shall be final and binding on the Parties.

5.5 Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek injunctive or other equitable relief from a court of competent jurisdiction in Kano State to protect its confidential information or intellectual property pending the resolution of any dispute under this Clause 5.

5.6 The obligation to pay any amount due and payable under this Agreement shall not be suspended or delayed by reason of any dispute, except as otherwise agreed in writing by the Parties.

**6. FORCE MAJEURE**

6.1 Neither Party shall be liable to the other for any failure or delay in the performance of its obligations under this Agreement, other than an obligation to pay money, if such failure or delay is caused by a Force Majeure Event.

6.2 For the purposes of this Agreement, a "Force Majeure Event" means any event or circumstance beyond the reasonable control of the affected Party, including but not limited to: acts of God; flood, drought, earthquake, or other natural disaster; epidemic or pandemic; act of terrorism or civil unrest; war or threat of war; fire or explosion; strikes or industrial action; and any law, regulation, order, or directive of any governmental authority that materially affects the performance of this Agreement.

6.3 The affected Party shall, as soon as reasonably practicable but in no event later than seven (7) days after the commencement of the Force Majeure Event, notify the other Party in writing of the nature of the event, its expected duration, and the obligations affected.

6.4 The affected Party shall use all reasonable efforts to mitigate the effects of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance of its obligations as soon as practicable. The Parties shall consult with each other to agree on reasonable alternative arrangements to minimize the impact of the Force Majeure Event on the implementation of the activities.
